canonical_answers: The angular frequency is 20.0 rad/s and maximum speed is 1.60 m/s.

payload.text: A 0.250 kg mass on an ideal 100 N/m spring oscillates with amplitude 0.080 m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict how the observable changes when the defining scale parameter is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

criteria.description: Doubling the amplitude leaves the angular frequency unchanged at ω = 20.0 rad/s, since ω = sqrt(k/m) depends only on k and m, but it doubles the maximum speed to 3.20 m/s, since v_max = ωA is directly proportional to amplitude.
required_evidence: angular frequency stays 20.0 rad/s because it does not depend on amplitude
maximum speed doubles to 3.20 m/s because v_max is proportional to amplitude
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show angular frequency stays 20.0 rad/s because it does not depend on amplitude; maximum speed doubles to 3.20 m/s because v_max is proportional to amplitude.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why assuming the spring is ideal and the oscillation undamped lets you use ω = sqrt(k/m) and v_max = ωA to obtain the angular frequency and maximum speed.

criteria.description: Correctly cites ω = sqrt(k/m) and v_max = ωA as the governing relations and states that the spring is assumed ideal and the motion undamped.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show ideal-spring assumption; v_max = omega times amplitude.
